o1.biggest_strength: Builds the series on the quiz split and the sunscreen click-to-order gap. Email 2 Version A pairs niacinamide with daily sunscreen for uneven tone, and Email 4 answers white cast and stickiness, using the dusky-skin review as proof.
o1.biggest_mistake: Email 5 tells everyone to use the salicylic acid wash morning and night. That contradicts Version C, which tells dry and sensitive people not to start with an acid, and it overloads beginners.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Branch Email 5 by skin concern instead of pushing all three products to everyone, and add a holdout test against today's single email so lift is proven.

o2.biggest_strength: Ready to launch. It shows revenue per click (₹48 vs ₹20 vs ₹9), sets entry and checkout-flow filters, offers A/B subject lines with character counts, includes a submit-ready WhatsApp Marketing template, and plans a 50/50 test against today's email.
o2.biggest_mistake: It invents a signer ('Mohit, Co-founder') for Email 5. Version A also doesn't tell dark-spot buyers to pair the serum with morning sunscreen, which is the core routine for that group. The sample-size claim of 4,700 per side to detect 18% to 20% is slightly optimistic.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Add morning sunscreen to the dark-spot version, give a fuller answer on stickiness in humid weather, and replace the invented signer with a confirmed name.

reason: Both read the data well. The second is more consistent from email to email, treats sensitive skin the same way all the way through, and comes with the Klaviyo filters, WhatsApp template and test plan I'd need to switch it on this week.
